summary: Polygon's curated list of the best horror movies available to stream, spanning old classics and recent hits across Netflix, Hulu, Max, Paramount Plus, Criterion Channel and others. Each entry lists director, cast, where to watch, and a short blurb from a Polygon writer. The latest update added the editor's pick, Sammo Hung's jiangshi martial arts comedy Encounters of the Spooky Kind.
one_line: Polygon's streaming guide to the best horror movies, from Night of the Living Dead to Us, with the editor's pick Encounters of the Spooky Kind.
key_facts: The latest update to the list added Encounters of the Spooky Kind, directed by Sammo Hung and streaming on the Criterion Channel.

In Encounters of the Spooky Kind, Sammo Hung directed, co-wrote, choreographed and stars as Bold Cheung, a pedicab driver; Yuen Biao plays the silent hopping vampire, and Sam Raimi reportedly ripped one of its fight sequences for Evil Dead II.
Alone, directed by John Hyams, is a woman-on-the-run thriller with a 98-minute running time, starring Jules Willcox as a recent widow named Jessica.
Annihilation (Alex Garland) follows scientists investigating The Shimmer, an area spreading from a meteor strike where creatures merge with unnaturally green vegetation; it streams on Netflix.
David Cronenberg's 2022 Crimes of the Future imagines humans unable to feel pain and spawning new organs, with Viggo Mortensen as performance artist Saul Tenser; Howard Shore composed the score.
Kiyoshi Kurosawa's 1997 film Cure follows detective Kenichi Takabe (Kōji Yakusho) investigating linked murders, with violence portrayed as a virus.
Clive Barker's 1987 directorial debut Hellraiser adapts his 1986 novella The Hellbound Heart and centers on the Lament Configuration puzzle box that summons Cenobites.
Bong Joon-ho's The Host was the highest-grossing South Korean film ever after its release and won Best Film at the Asian Film Awards and the Blue Dragon Film Awards.
John Carpenter's In the Mouth of Madness is the third in his apocalypse trilogy, alongside The Thing and Prince of Darkness.
Night of the Living Dead came out a month before the MPAA rating system and was never copyrighted, putting it in the public domain due to a distributor error.
Andrzej Żuławski's 1981 film Possession, set in Cold War West Berlin and starring Sam Neill and Isabelle Adjani, was inspired by his own 1976 divorce.

Egor Abramenko's 2020 debut Sputnik is set in 1983, with psychiatrist Tatyana treating a cosmonaut who hosts an alien organism; it was slated for the 2020 Tribeca Film Festival before going to video-on-demand due to COVID-19.
Tobe Hooper's 1974 The Texas Chain Saw Massacre made over $30 million on a budget of around $140,000, runs 83 minutes, and has been followed by eight films, including a 2022 Netflix version.
Unfriended (2014, Levan Gabriadze) takes place entirely on a laptop screen during a Skype call, with a presence called 'billie227'; the sequel is Unfriended: Dark Web.
Jordan Peele's 2019 film Us features doppelgängers called the Tethered, with Lupita Nyong'o and an extremely brief but standout role by Elisabeth Moss.
